#image("/imgs/ap-calc-ab-2011-form-b-frq-03-diagram-01.png", width: 65%)

The functions $f$ and $g$ are given by $f(x)= sqrt(x)$ and $g(x)= 6 - x$. Let $R$ be the region bounded by the $x$-axis and the graphs of $f$ and $g$, as shown in the figure above.

(a) Find the area of $R$.

(b) The region $R$ is the base of a solid. For each $y$, where $0 <= y <= 2$, the cross section of the solid taken perpendicular to the $y$-axis is a rectangle whose base lies in $R$ and whose height is $2 y$. Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression that gives the volume of the solid.

(c) There is a point $P$ on the graph of $f$ at which the line tangent to the graph of $f$ is perpendicular to the graph of $g$. Find the coordinates of point $P$.
